stem: Who was the author of Tabaqat-i-Nasiri?
expl: The author of ‘Tabaqat-i-Nasiri’ was Minhaj-us-Siraj, and it was dedicated to Sultan Nasiruddin. This work has 23 chapters. H. G. Raverty translated it into English. This book contains a direct account of Muhammad Ghori’s conquest of India. It is noteworthy that Minhaj stated that Qutbuddin Aibak issued coins in his own name and had the khutba read.

stem: The account of the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta is known as

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Ibn Battuta was a resident of Morocco in Africa, who came to Delhi during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. He wrote his travel account in the Arabic language in a book titled Rihla (Rehla). He criticized the policies of Muhammad Tughlaq’s period.
‘Barahmasa’ was composed by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. Among Jayasi’s works—‘Padmavat’, ‘Akharavat’, and ‘Aakhiri Kalam’—‘Padmavat’ holds an important place in Hindi literature.

stem: Which great saint wrote the book Gyan Deepak?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Saint Dariya Saheb composed the book titled ‘Gyan Deepak’. He was from Bihar. Salar Masood Ghazi was the head of Mahmud of Ghazni’s army. His dargah is located at Bahraich in Uttar Pradesh.

options.label: d

expl: Chachnama was translated into Persian by Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi. Chachnama is a book written in the Arabic language. Clear information about the author’s name is not available. Chachnama contains an account of the history of Sindh from 680 to 718 C.E. A complete translation from Persian into English was done in 1900 A.D. by Mirza Kalichbeg Fredunbeg.
‘Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi’ is the title of two separate Persian works written by Shams-e-Siraj Afif and Ziauddin Barani, which have the same title. In the given options, option (a) is the correct answer.
